description: The diary documents the daily activities of William Healey Dall and his colleagues in the Scientific Corps on the Western Union Telegraph Expedition while in San Francisco, California as well as during their field work in Alaska. Entries are dated from January 1, 1866 to May 25, 1867. First entries describe daily work while in California including writing reports, studying specimens, preparations and acquisition of equipment for field work, personal activities, and weather. Later entries describe travel by ship to Alaska, observed marine life and birds, specimens collected and prepared (including fossils), illustrations of accommodations, personal and professional interactions with local inhabitants and expedition participants including participating Russians, as well as personal impressions. In the middle of the book, miscellaneous lists are included such as a cash account, a list of letters sent, a list of recipients of a copy of Memorial on Bridges to other papers, and synopses of letters of importance.

This diary kept between approximately 5 February to 29 April 1900 contains photo identifications, expense accounts, and miscellaneous notes from Stejneger's trip to Puerto Rico and the West Indies. Notes are narrative and mostly describe the events of the day with only some mention of collecting birds, lizards, and bats.

This field book contains entries from April 1899 to November 1899. It includes an itinerary of Bailey's travels through Texas and California describing the observation and collection of specimens by Bailey in Washington D.C. and also contains miscellaneous notes from 1913, 1915, notes made on trip to the Patuxent River, Maryland, April 23-24, 1916.
This item contains sparse entries from 1899, 1900, 1915 and 1916. Entries are dated and include scientific names and localities.

These includes the various original invoices and other official papers of the U. S. Exploring Expedition. Included are correspondence, specimen lists, and invoices. There are varying amounts of information given in the correspondence relating to the shipments of specimens. They generally describe contents, main type of element collected, sometimes information about the collector. Lists sometimes give collecting location and description. Correspondence also relates lists of sketches that were sent back, including descriptions. Materials include official letters to Capt. Wilkes, 1839 - 1840, mostly transmitting shipping lists of specimens, and some loose sheets from the purser's account book, 1838; original invoices of shells, 1839 - 1840; original invoices of miscellaneous specimens, 1839 - 1841; original invoices and catalogue of geological and mineralogical specimens, 1839 - 1840. There are several references to Orange Harbour.

The memorabilia of the Presidential Cruise of 1938 collected by Waldo Schmitt, and include naval orders of the day, that indicate times for activities (including collecting), locations anchored, visitors,and press releases of discoveries and shipboard activities. Additionally includes memorabilia from Shellback ceremony and extra curricular activities. Covers the locations visited during the cruise in the Galapagos [Archipiélago de Colón], Panama, Mexico, Costa Rica.

The miscellaneous notes are the result of work completed by Waldo Schmitt during the Alaska King Crab Investigation, 1940. Information recorded includes statistics for collecting sites (average weight, width and length of male and ovig and nonovig females), notes about canneries, progress reports, tables from tagging, and dated notes for sites. Locations are through out the vicinity of the Aleutian Islands in Alaska.

Miscellaneous materials document the processes and results of Waldo Schmitt's work during the Alaska King Crab Investigation, 1940. Materials include program of work (including instructions for hydrographic and biological observations); list of supplies; plans for future work; comments and recommendations on work completed and process to complete investigation.

Miscellaneous materials document the processes and results of Waldo Schmitt's work during the Alaska King Crab Investigation, 1940. Materials include dated notes listing issues with work, equipment, locations, investigation participants, and methods and results of specimen collecting. There is more than one set of dated notes -- up to three related entries to a given date. There are drafts of correspondence for use of equipment in Alitak Bay. Locations are through out the Aleutian Islands of Alaska.

Notes were recorded by Waldo Schmitt during the United States Navy Galapagos Expedition, 1941. Includes plans and specifications for a proposed field laboratory in the Galapagos Islands to study the wildlife and environment. Includes lists of aniticipated supplies needed, structure of Smithsonian and Ecuadorean Government partnership, proposal of specific types of observations to be conducted; drafts of agreements; cost estimates; and proposed sites.

Includes assorted notes about collecting various types of specimens and requests of Smithsonian departments during the Smithsonian-Bredin Belgian Congo Expedition, 1955, led by Waldo Schmitt. Includes notes about observations and information about local inhabitants, notes about fish and wildlife observed, list of research stations visited, itinerary version with notes after locations visited, and drafts of correspondence about film and expedition arrangements.

Assorted notes document Waldo Schmitt's work during the Smithsonian-Bredin Caribbean Expedition, 1956. Includes a calendar with short daily entries about events. Loose notes given details about decisions made during expedition about anchorage locations, descriptions of sights, history of specific islands, a list of possible yacht anchorages, receipts, yacht charter agreement.

The miscellaneous notes documents Waldo Schmitt's work during the Smithsonian-Bredin Society Islands Expedition, 1957. Includes descriptions of local inhabitants and long term residents that Waldo worked with, who gave information about the islands, notes about soil samples (including numbers, location, date and location description), drafts of correspondence, and notes and copied citations of reference texts (some copied texts of history of region). Locations covered in French Polynesia Society Islands [Îles de la Société] include Bora-Bora.

The miscellaneous notes documents the work of Waldo Schmitt during the Smithsonian-Bredin Caribbean Expedition, 1958. Includes notes about historic events on islands visited, shipment of gear and specimens to the National Museum of Natural History, specifications of a possibly used sailing vessel, and notes about soil samples collected that include location, numbers, and descriptions of collecting environments. Locations in the Caribbean includes the vicinity of Barbuda, Antigua, and Virgin Gorda.

Expense accounts and receipts document the work completed by Waldo Schmitt during the Smithsonian-Bredin Caribbean Expedition, 1960 [Smithsonian-Bredin Expedition to Yucatan (1960)]. Includes a chronological itemized list of miscellaneous expenses. Includes details about participants and related locations, with dates. Includes information about bays and other locations on the islands that were visited. Locations in Mexico include the vicinity of Progreso and Cozumel.

The miscellaneous notes document the work of Waldo Schmitt during the Smithsonian-Bredin Caribbean Expedition, 1960 [Smithsonian-Bredin Expedition to Yucatan (1960)]. Includes two news clippings. Some notes are dated and are journal style, drafts of correspondence. Describes travel progress on sailing vessel, status following itinerary, working relationship with participants, weather conditions including wind directions and speeds and temperatures, descriptions of terrain and structures in port, and work completed during expedition. Locations in Mexico include vicinity of Mujeres and Cozumel Island.

Miscellaneous notes document Waldo L. Schmitt's work during the Palmer Peninsula (Antarctica) Survey, 1962-1963. Notes cover observations about graduate students working on site, notebook covering his work done at the McMurdo Station on Ross Island. Notes describe laboratory space, staff (by name), equipment, methods, station conditions, and scheduling of fieldwork locations.

The Waldo Schmitt's miscellaneous notes are from his work during the Palmer Peninsula (Antarctica) Survey, 1962-1963. Many of the notes relate to judging the suitability of sites for collecting, conditions during collecting, and dates of these observations. Some notes consist of lists, others are journal style in structure. Many have related dates. Some notes include citations or brief summaries of 19th and 20th century collecting/expedition history of the area. Locations discussed often include not just islands but also their bays, coves, and harbors. Includes notes on Deception Island, memo of procedures for aboard USS Staten Island (AGB-5), program notes on criteria for site selection, and map indicating selected sites of interest. These include South Shetland Islands, Hope Bay, Snow Hill-Cape Longing, D. De Gerlache Strait,E. Grandidier Channel, F. Marin Darbel Bay, and Adelaide Island.

Miscellaneous notes and maps cover work completed by Waldo Schmitt during the Palmer Peninsula (Antarctica) Survey, 1962-1963. Notes come in a variety of forms including a "general abstracted narrative from Capt. MacDonald's notes" that includes dates, destinations, water conditions, air and water temperatures, and overview of daily activities of participants; copies of naval messages from USS Staten Island (AGB-5) detail work about collecting topographical data and collecting; list of bottom samples collected, with location and depth included; notes for recognizing types of penguins; and history of region and personal opinions. Maps have hand written notes about locations. Locations included are throughout the islands surrounding Palmer Peninsula, including Adelaide Island, Hope Bay, Argentine Island, Discovery Bay, and Admiralty Bay among others.

Miscellaneous notes cover work completed by Waldo Schmitt during the Palmer Peninsula (Antarctica) Survey, 1962-1963. Includes notes about selection of landing sites (terrain, water accessibility) and materials collected and by whom (some including references to fossils). Locations discussed include bases in Dorian Bay, Paradise Harbor, Lockroy, and Arthur Seymour Island, Dorian Bay and Snow Hill.

These are M. Moynihan's miscellaneous observation notes on primates, 1965. Includes a sketch, map of forest near Valparaíso in Caquetá, Colombia including the primate colonies, and sketch of two primates. Includes table with links between Sag.g., C-mico.g., C-ubus m. Observation notes are organized by type of primate and indicate whether present, population abundance, demographics (sex and number of adults), and behaviors; and notes on correlation of primate cries and type. Some information is unidentified.

This is 1 of 2 folders of M. Moynihan's observations of mixed flocks, 1958-1964. Pages are numbered. Entries are headed with location, date, and type. Observations describe appearance, behavior, interactions, and calls of individual and groupings of birds. Includes sex, time of day, environment, elevation, and a list of attempted copulations. There are illustrations of birds and notations indicated by color and pattern. Locations include Bronx Zoo; Cerro Punta, Cerro Campana, Barro Colorado, Arraiján, Panama; Unduavi, Bolivia; Pichincha, Ecuador; Tarma and Iquitos, Peru.

This is 2 of 2 folders of M. Moynihan's observations of mixed flocks, 1958-1959, 1961-1962, 1964. Pages are numbered. Entries are headed with date, location, and type. Observations describe the behavior, appearance calls of individual, pairs, and groups of birds. Descriptions include time of day, sex, and descriptions of mated pairs. Illustrations of birds augment the text, and notations indicated by color and pattern. Locations include Cerro Campana, Cerro Punta, Frijoles, Barro Colorado, Panama; Unduavi, Bolivia; Quito, Iñaquito, Pichincha, Ecuador; Bogota, Colombia; Iquitos, Peru; and London Zoo, Washington Zoo, and Bronx Zoo.

The notes document M. Moynihan's observations of monkeys, 1964, 1967-1970. There are two sets of page numbers and includes some typed materials. Includes typed and handwritten material. Entries are headed with date, location and type. Observations cover appearance, behavior and calls, and include reference to sites previously observed by Alexander Wetmore; includes information like sex, time of day, and description of habitat, elevation, weather, vegetation. Includes illustrations of primates augmenting text and notations indicated by pattern. Comments on observations are broken out from the text. At the end of materials are tables of data from observations. Locations include Barro Colorado Island and Puerto Armuelles, Panama; Colombia (La Deseo, Valparaíso, El Pepino, Santa Rosa, Puerto Umbría).

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 28 March 1929 to 27 April 1931 in Ireland. Most specimens collected were insects, primarily hymenoptera. Other types of specimens may have been collected. Stelfox lists the name of the specimen, date collected, sex, quantity, sometimes remarks on the weather, location, sometimes specific type of environment, sometimes remarks about which specimens he would like to collect, sometimes additional information. Some specimens were collected by R. A. Phillips. Localities include, but are not limited to Gold Mine Valley, Lugnaquilla, Arklow, Deer Park, Kilcoole, Kilcarry Bridge, and Canterbury. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. “List of ichneumons and braconids sent to S. A. Roman in Nov. 1929 (not. Jan 1930!)” (starting on page 100), numbers 75-117, is also included, as well as miscellaneous inserts containing field notes.

Other types of specimens may have been collected. Stelfox lists the name of the specimen, date collected, sex, quantity, sometimes remarks on the weather, location, sometimes specific type of environment, sometimes remarks about which specimens he would like to collect, sometimes additional information. Some specimens were collected by R. A. Phillips. Localities include, but are not limited to Lucan, Rathdrum, Glendun, Enniskerry (currently Áth na Sceire), Duncannon, and Bundoran. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. “List of specimens sent to S. Roman November 1931 [continued from vol. 3, p. 106]”, numbers 118-145, is also included, as well as miscellaneous inserts containing field notes. Correspondence about specimens from A. Roman to Stelfox is also included.

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 1 June 1926 to 27 March 1929 in mostly Wicklow and Dublin Counties, Ireland. Most specimens collected were insects, primarily hymenoptera. Other types of specimens may have been collected. Stelfox lists the name of the specimen, date collected, sex, quantity, sometimes remarks on the weather, location, sometimes specific type of environment, sometimes remarks about which specimens he would like to collect, sometimes additional information. Some specimens were collected by R. A. Phillips. Localities include, but are not limited to Arklow, Rathdrum, Kilbarrack, Powerscourt, and Cloghoge Glen. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. “List of ichneumon sent to S. Roman, 14/2/28. See also in letter dated 24/2/28”, with numbers 35-74, is also included, as well as miscellaneous inserts containing field notes.

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 16 August 1944 to 8 August 1946 in Ireland. A note on the title page reads "Kerry trip May-June 1946 in next volume". Most specimens collected were insects, primarily hymenoptera. Other types of specimens may have been collected. Notes on botanical specimens observed and possibly collected are also included. Stelfox lists the name of the specimen, date collected, sex, quantity, sometimes remarks on the weather, location, sometimes specific type of environment, sometimes remarks about which specimens he would like to collect, sometimes additional information. Localities include, but are not limited to Glenasmole, Athdown, Royal Canal, Rye Water, Phoenix Park, Merrion Square, and Bellina. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. A photograph of Glen of Aherlow, Galtee Mountains (west end and centre), Co. Tipperary taken by the Irish Tourist Association, Inc and miscellaneous notes are inserted at the title page. A small sketched map of Killiney Bay and notes of specimens collected by Philip Harwood are inserted at page 76.

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 28 May 1946 to 12 May 1948 in Scotland and Ireland. Most specimens collected were insects, primarily hymenoptera. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. Miscellaneous notes and notes on specimens “collected for me by R. C. Faris (ofGaran) when on holiday at Dunderan, Oct. 1946, are also included.

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 20 August 1952 to 18 August 1953 in Ireland. Specimens collected or observed are mostly insects, primarily hymenoptera, but botanical specimens are also included. Stelfox lists the name of the specimen, date collected, sex, quantity, sometimes remarks on the weather, location, sometimes specific type of environment, sometimes remarks about which specimens he would like to collect, sometimes additional information. Localities include but are not limited to Kitalown in Tallaght, Royal Canal, Glending in Kildare, Oldtown, Killoughter, Yellow Corrie, and Ben Lawer. Botanical specimens affixed to pages 49, 50, and 185, and inserted at page 142. Miscellaneous notes and memo from Max Fischer to Stelfox inserted at the end of the journal.

This field book contains field notes of collections Stelfox made from 23 August 1953 to 25 July 1954 in Ireland. 'R.C.L.P' following a name signifies that specimen were seen and verified by D. R. C. L. Perkins, F.R.S. A Botanical specimen affixed to a label, photograph of Marcus W. R. de V. Graham, and miscellaneous notes are inserted at page 161.

An inserted table of contents contains a full listing of localities. This field book contains a specimen list of botanical specimens collected from 25 November 1945 to 9 June 1946 in various locations within the following states and island groups: Virginia, Illinois, Pennsylvania, California, Hawai’i, the Marshall Islands, the Caroline Islands, and the Mariana Islands. Collector numbers 24225 – 24941 are included. Occasionally, notes become long and narrative. Specimen list includes scientific name, date, locality, collector number, and sometimes physical description of the specimen that includes its measurements, color, and other information. Miscellaneous notes, a memo from Dr. John A. Stevenson to Fosberg, and a map of Tinian (Mariana Islands) marked with collecting station locations is inserted in the front of the book.

An inserted table of contents contains a full listing of localities and corresponding collector numbers. This field book contains a specimen list of botanical specimens collected from 6-24 August 1946 in various locations within the Caroline Islands and the Marshall Islands. Collector numbers 26154 – 26789 are included. Occasionally, notes become long and narrative, and will sometimes include general descriptions of area vegetation. Specimen list includes scientific name, date, locality, collector number, and sometimes physical description of the specimen that includes its measurements, color, and other information. Caroline Islands localities include various collecting stations on Nukuoro Atoll, Ponape, Kusaie (Lela or Lele Island), and Jaluit Atoll. Marshall Islands localities include Kwajalein Atoll. List of Islets of Nukuoro Atoll (south to north) inserted between pages 24 and 25. Four small sheets of miscellaneous notes are inserted in the back of the book.

Localities include but are not limited to Virginia, Maryland, and Connecticut in the Continental United States, Fiji, New Caledonia, and several locations in New Zealand (including North and South Island). The 1962-1963 travelogue documents Doris Cochran’s National Science Foundation funded trip to visit museums in South America and collect frog specimens, building on collections she made there in 1935. Includes summary of events, itinerary, and narrative entries on daily activities. Narrative entries include description of surrounding flora and fauna and references to specific collections of herpetological specimens collected. Includes miscellaneous clippings and business card in the back of the book. Localities included in this trip include Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo in Brazil, Bogota in Colombia, Isla Barro Colorado (Barro Colorado Island) in Panama, Argentina, Peru, and several other localities.

The journal documents Florence Bailey's travel and observations in Maine, 1911. In the front of the volume is a loose insert listing locations, vegetation, types of habitat, birds observed. Pages are numbered. Entries are not continuous. There are often blank pages in-between. Some journal entries are dated, others headed with type of environment (pastures, cranberry bog, [type of tree] swamps), type of plant (ferns, flowers), or name of town. They begin June 23, 1911 and are often headed with location. They describe travel from Washington to Maine with time in Canada (Montreal), travel details (mode of transportation, accommodations), observations of vegetation, descriptions of behavior and appearance of birds. Some lists of vegetation include notes about descriptions and habitat, and sometimes date. There is a miscellaneous heading describing other fauna observed (insects, snakes). Locations include Fryeburg Harbor and North Waterford.

Notebook containing miscellaneous and some field notes from Whitmore's trips to the Galapagos, Mexico, and China. Notes from the Galapagos include a brief list of bones from July 1972 collected at Darwin Station. Notes include color and length of bones. Film log of images taken of specimens from Mexico are also included. Also included are meeting notes from meetings and conferences.

This item consists of a folder of data collected at sea by Pacific Ocean Biological Survey Program staff, 1966 on the Miscellaneous Pelagic Cruise No. 5, aboard the U.S.C.G.C. Basswood. The cruise began in Honolulu, Hawaii and ended in Guam. The cruise visited localities in the Marshall Islands including: Majuro Atoll, Kwajalein Atoll, and Eniwetok [Enewetak] Atoll. Materials include: bird observation sheets, fix data sheets, and climatological data sheets. Bird observation sheets include time, species, #, dir., hgt., remarks, and noon position. Remarks include physical descriptions of birds (colors, size, maturity), flock size, and behavior (sitting on water, feeding, etc.). Additional bird observation data include counts for: total flocks, feeding flocks, traveling flocks, total birds, and bird counts by species. Fix data sheets include date, time and position data, distance data, time of fix, type of fix, longitude, and latitude. Climatological data includes time, lat., long., pres wea, vis, slp, dry b, wet b, dew pt, hum%, tl sky, opa sky, waves, sea temp, wind s, wind d, course, speed. Also included is a typed report.

Remarks include physical descriptions of birds (colors, size, maturity), flock size, and behavior (sitting on water, feeding, etc.). Fix data sheets include date, time and position data, distance data, time of fix, type of fix, longitude, and latitude. The field notes document the ornithological field work of Joshua F. B. Camblos in Virginia. Time and location include 1932-1939 (includes egg collecting at Big Stone Gap, Parramore Island, and Wachapreague, 1932-1936; nesting of Bald Eagles in Princess Anne County [now part of Virginia Beach], 1937-1939; bird observations, 1932-1938). Notes are a mix of handwritten and typed, and there are a wide variety of information and formats. These include but are not limited to a list on Camblos's egg collection that list type of bird (common and scientific name), A.O.U. No., and date; quotes from texts; table of data headed by date and list type (common name), no., no. in set, inc., size, date, location (includes additional location about landmarks e.g. old reservoir); descriptions of eggs collected that list name, date, no., inc., sizes, situation ("situation" describes habitat, vegetation, nest composition where collected); journal entries from series of trips to observe the nesting of bald eagles in Princess Anne County, Virginia; miscellaneous descriptions of migrating birds, nests of young, etc.; table of average sizes and date when fresh eggs may be obtained in the state of Virginia (with maps).

The notebook documents the work of H. S. Ladd in Lau, Fiji, January 1 - October 18, 1934. The volume begins with a table of contents listing expenses, daily log, government officials etc., contributions, miscellaneous Fijian names, and record of collections. Daily log entries are dated and describe daily activities, work with colleagues, travel details, weather, routes traveled, field work and collecting sites, and office work.

Branches of blossoming plum in contrasting inlays of lead and luminous mother-of-pearl form a continuous design that extends over the sides and lid of this box. Koetsu's (1558-1637) innovations in lacquer designs are well documented. The decoration on this box, however, appears to have been based not on an original design by Koetsu, but on the motifs printed in mica on the covers of the woodblock-printed libretti for No performances that were produced after 1604 by the wealthy merchant and scholar Suminokura Soan (1571-1632), in collaboration with Koetsu. The books displayed in this care are examples of the books, known as Sagabon, published by Soan and often based on Koetsu's calligraphy and designs.

This mask represents a demon (oni). It probably was used in tsuina (or oni yarai), a ritual exorcism performed on the night before the New Year to drive out demons. The eyes once may have been covered with gilt metal to create a gleaming, fearsome appearance.

Whistler’s good friend Henri Fantin-Latour originally included this portrait as part of a large composition called Le toast: Hommage à la Verit&‌eacute; (The Toast: Homage to Truth) that also depicted such avant-garde figures as the painter Edouard Manet and the poet Charles Baudelaire. The Frenchmen wore conventional black suits in the group portrait. Whistler, however, insisted on distinguishing himself by wearing a colorful Chinese robe. Fantin’s group portrait and Whistler’s painting The Princess from the Land of Porcelain were exhibited at the Paris Salon of 1865. Critics ridiculed Fantin’s work, and he later destroyed it, leaving only this fragment of Whistler.

Since at least the second century, Indian sculptors created ivory thrones to proclaim royal command. On this splendidly carved throne leg, a gajasimha--a mythical creature combining the strength of an elephant (gaja) and a lion (simha)--calmly dispatches the demonic warrior dangling from its trunk. The sculptor contrasted the forceful curves and broad smooth surfaces of the elephant-lion with an intricately realized mountain landscape. Archers and wildlife gambol through its crags, while a hermit meditates and a lion slumbers.

The pleasing visual contrast achieved by applying pigment-based designs and drawings to an unadorned natural surface--silk, paper, clay, or wood--expresses an important aspect of Japanese aesthetic sensibility: the celebration of art's material foundations.
